title: Version binding policy: tag/semver/hash precedence and SDK surface
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers need deterministic behavior when they specify a model in the API/SDK. Current semantics are ambiguous across selector types (tag, semver range, exact semver, commit hash) and do not guarantee a stable performance profile. This ticket defines the canonical precedence rules, SDK surface, runtime fallback behavior, and how performance profile publishing ties to pinned model versions. Scope: SDK input surface, API validation errors, runtime resolver precedence, telemetry for ambiguous resolutions, and rollout notes for migration. Out of scope: UI changes in Console (separate PM ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Precedence rule implemented: commit-hash > exact-semver > semver-range > annotated-tag > alias/latest. SDK and control-plane perform identical resolution and return stable resolver metadata in response headers.
SDK accepts a single canonical selector string and rejects ambiguous multi-selector inputs with a clear error code (400 + code MODEL_PIN_AMBIGUOUS).

When a model is pinned, the runtime binds the matching performance_profile_id and includes it in the request-level metadata. If no compatible profile exists, runtime falls back to the latest compatible profile and emits a warning event; the call still succeeds unless profile compatibility is explicitly required by the customer.
All resolution paths are covered by unit tests and an integration test that simulates tag movement and semver range resolution over time.
Telemetry records selector type, resolved ref (hash/semver), whether fallback occurred, and latency/cost delta compared to expected profile. Telemetry exported to the pin-resolution dashboard.
Migration docs and SDK changelog entry published before release.
API error messages documented and surfaced in the SDK with actionable remediation steps.
decision_log: 2026-03-06: Chose deterministic precedence (hash > exact semver > semver range > tag > latest) to favor reproducibility.
2026-03-07: Require performance profiles to be versioned and referenced by profile_id; profile binding is recorded in resolution metadata.
2026-03-09: SDK API will accept a single selector string with optional explicit profile: e.g., 'model:v2.1' or 'model@sha:abcdef'. Multi-selector inputs will be deprecated.
2026-03-10: Fallback policy: if profile mismatch, use conservative profile with lower throughput expectations but stricter correctness. Emit telemetry and a warning header.
implementation_notes: API: add resolver endpoint /v1/models/resolve?selector=<string> that returns resolved_ref, resolved_profile_id, resolution_path, and warning flags.
SDK: expose ModelSelector.parse(selector) helper and ModelClient.resolve(selector) which returns a deterministic Resolution object (stringified in response metadata).
Runtime: implement resolver cache keyed by (selector, tenant, region) with TTL 5m and invalidation hooks on model publish/tag events.
Runtime fallback: implement 'conservative profile' store that contains guarded defaults for latency/throughput if profile resolution fails. Use this path only when profile compatibility checks fail.

Edge cases: pre-release semver (1.2.0-beta) matches only exact semver unless explicitly allowed with an allow-prerelease flag; wildcard ranges follow semver spec; numeric range resolution chooses highest semver that satisfies the range and is not marked deprecated.
Backward compatibility: preserve existing SDK 'model' parameter behavior for one release with a deprecation warning header.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): add resolver endpoint and SDK preview to internal customers. Collect telemetry for 2 weeks.
Phase 2 (opt-in): ship SDK that uses new resolver when opt_in flag is set. Surface deprecation warnings for old behavior.
Phase 3 (default): flip new resolver on by default and keep old resolver for 30 days behind a feature flag for emergency rollback.
Phase 4: remove old resolver and finalize docs after observability confirms no major regressions.
tests_and_checks: Unit tests for selector parsing: tag, exact semver, semver range, commit hash, alias.
Integration test that simulates tag reassignment and verifies that a commit-hash pinned client is unaffected while tag-pinned clients see a change.
Load test for resolver cache under 10k resolves/sec to ensure TTL and invalidation do not thrash downstream services.
E2E test validating that resolved_profile_id is present in runtime logs and returned in SDK response metadata.
Chaos test: publish a new model with incompatible profile and ensure runtime falls back to conservative profile and emits warning events.
